references.text: Moses was asked by God at the burning bush, and in [ref:2 Mos 3:2|Exodus 3:2] we see the question of authority and commissioning – a theme that recurs when religious leaders ask Jesus about his authority.
In [ref:Luk 20:1|Luke 20:1] the context is described: Jesus was teaching in the temple and preaching the gospel, which prompted the chief priests and scribes to question his authority.

The parallel account in [ref:Matt 21:23-27|Matthew 21:23–27] recounts the same event where the chief priests and elders of the people ask Jesus by what authority he does these things, and who gave him this authority.

[ref:Mark 11:28-33|Mark 11:28–33] is the second synoptic parallel, where religious leaders pose the same question about Jesus’ authority, and Jesus responds with a counter-question concerning John’s baptism.
In [ref:Joh 2:18|John 2:18] the Jews ask Jesus a similar question after the temple cleansing: "What sign do you show us, since you do these things?" – the same demand to legitimize one’s authority.

In [ref:Apg 4:7|Acts 4:7] the council members ask Peter and John: "By what power or in whose name have you done this?" – the same pattern where religious authorities challenge the authority of those acting on God’s behalf.
In [ref:Apg 7:27|Acts 7:27] the man who wronged his neighbor asks Moses: "Who made you a ruler and judge over us?" – again, a question about who has granted authority.

In [ref:Joh 5:27|John 5:27] Jesus says that the Father has given the Son authority to execute judgment because he is the Son of Man. This indirectly answers the question of who gave Jesus his authority.
In [ref:Matt 28:18|Matthew 28:18] the risen Jesus declares: "All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me" – the final answer to the question about his authority and who granted it.
